62/S0.subgoal: Explain why external scripting support is necessary to achieve a customized experience in a development environment.

62/S1.subgoal: Describe the technical environment and role of scripting (C#) as a customizable component within the Unity development environment.

62/S2.subgoal: Demonstrate the initial steps required to create and integrate a script into a Unity project.

62/S3.subgoal: Detail the basic anatomy of a scripting file, including its components like namespace, class, Start, and Update functions.

62/S4.subgoal: Understand how to handle and observe data types and variables within scripts using the Inspector and Console.

62/S5.subgoal: Explain how to control object lifecycle and destroy game objects using specific functions in the scripting environment.

62/S6.subgoal: Classify and differentiate between various types of event functions, such as Update, GUI, and Physics events, and explain their purpose.

62/S7.subgoal: Describe the control flow mechanism of event functions, detailing when and how execution passes to and from the script.

62/S8.subgoal: Outline the procedure for instantiating prefabs dynamically at runtime by attaching scripts and referencing assets.

62/S9.subgoal: Differentiate between conditional statements (if-else) and how they are used to control script logic.

62/S10.subgoal: Compare and contrast the types of control flow loops (entry-controlled, exit-controlled, and for-each) available in scripting.

62/S11.subgoal: Describe how the Transform property allows programmatic manipulation of an object's position, rotation, and scale.

62/S12.subgoal: Explain the concept and necessity of using coroutines to spread tasks across multiple frames for time-based effects.

62/S13.subgoal: Describe how to utilize the InvokeRepeating function to execute a method repeatedly at specified time intervals.

62/S14.subgoal: List the various ways scripting supports user interaction and input, including device-specific inputs.

62/S15.subgoal: Detail the practical steps and settings required to compile and deploy a system using the Unity editor interface.

62/S16.subgoal: Understand the architectural need for importing external SDKs when the built-in features of the Unity environment are insufficient.

62/S17.subgoal: Introduce and justify the role of specialized SDKs, using Vuforia as an example, for enhancing native platform capabilities.

62/S18.subgoal: List the basic process for integrating a third-party SDK into the Unity development environment.

62/S19.subgoal: Describe the specific configuration steps required to set up an SDK like Vuforia for image recognition tasks.

62/S20.subgoal: Assemble the final Augmented Reality scene by integrating 3D models with targeted images and necessary behavior scripts.

62/S21.subgoal: Configure specific platform settings within the editor to ensure the successful build and deployment of the system.

62/S22.subgoal: Illustrate how an integrated SDK enables a marker-based AR system to recognize images and display corresponding digital content.

62/S23.subgoal: Summarize the key methods—scripting, building, and SDK incorporation—for extending the functionality of a development environment.

62/S24.subgoal: Recap the core concepts of linking theoretical knowledge to practical implementation in virtual and augmented reality systems.
